rows.rationale: KA-C5-006 (effective 2025-12-01) supersedes KA-C5-001's 17.5kW threshold with a 50kWp threshold for check meters. | Clause 4 concerns transformer capacity limits and deemed feasibility, not check meter requirements. | Check meter required only for >50kWp; proposed 45kWp system does not trigger this requirement.

KA-C5-006#cl-18 requires check meter for systems >50kWp, but proposed capacity is 45kWp which is below threshold, so clause does not trigger rejection. | KA-C5-006#cl-4 concerns transformer capacity limits and deemed feasibility for <150kW systems; it does not support rejection for check meter absence.

Registry shows GJ-C3-001#cl-13.5 is superseded as of 2025-07-07; generator should cite GJ-C3-003#cl-13.5-check instead. | System is exactly 20 kW, so check meter is optional not mandatory; approval cannot be based on mandatory check meter requirement.

System capacity is exactly 20 kW, so check meter is optional per clause; since check meter is 'Not provided', this should not block or approve but the rule citation is misapplied. | Application lacks required Solar Check Meter documentation but generator approved without verifying meter compliance for the 20 kW threshold boundary condition.

60kWp capacity is under 150kW, so KA-C5-006#cl-4-note-ii deems it feasible without SDO verification, making approval premature while Technical Feasibility is still pending. | Cited clause requires SDO to verify and issue intimation letter, but portal shows Technical Feasibility outcome not yet communicated, so approval is unsupported.

The cited clause establishes deemed feasibility, not automatic approval; Technical Feasibility has not been communicated by DISCOM, so approval cannot be granted yet. | SDO must verify technical feasibility and issue intimation letter before approval; this step is incomplete per portal status.
Clause GJ-C3-001#cl-13.5 was superseded by GJ-C3-003 amendment effective 2020-01-22, before application date 2025-09-03.

The cited clause requires Solar Meter accuracy of 1.0 class or better; the proposal shows 0.2S which exceeds requirements, but the decision cites meter accuracy as approval reason rather than addressing the actual blocking issue. | Proposed 8 kWp system exceeds sanctioned load of 5 kW; capacity eligibility rules were not evaluated for approval decision.

DL-C3-004#cl-3.8 was superseded by DL-C3-009#cl-3.8 effective 2024-04-01, before the application date of 2024-08-04. | The applicable rule allows GNM capacity up to 5x sanctioned load (max 10MW); 12MW exceeds 10MW cap, but correct rule was not cited.
Proposed 12000 kWp is within 5× sanctioned load (5×3000=15000 kW) and under 10 MW max, so the capacity limit is satisfied, not violated.

UP-C3-001 was superseded by UP-C3-002 effective 2019-01-04, before the application date of 2023-08-08. | Proposed 1.0 kWp does not exceed 100% of 2.0 kW sanctioned load, so rejection is unsupported by applicable regulation.

Clause 5.1 only validates capacity limits; it does not authorize approval while application is still at 'Technical Feasibility' workflow stage. | No subsidy calculation or central subsidy scheme eligibility was evaluated despite residential rooftop solar typically qualifying for PM-KUSUM or MNRE subsidies.

The clause from GJ-C3-001 was superseded as of the application date (2025-01-03); the amended GJ-C3-003#cl-13.5-check should apply. | Check meter is mandatory but absence should not cause rejection; DISCOM installs it at consumer cost per regulation.
The clause mandates check meters for systems >20kW, but EPC proposal shows 'Solar Check Meter: Not provided' is a documentation gap, not a rejection ground—DISCOM installs meters per the regulation.

KA-C5-006#cl-18 (effective 2025-12-01) supersedes KA-C5-001#cl-15, raising check meter threshold to 50kWp. | Generator should have applied the newer 50kWp threshold; 80kWp system requires check meter under current rules.

The cited clause requires a check meter for systems >50kWp; the 80kWp system lacks one, but EPC proposal states 'Not provided' which is a documentation gap, not grounds for outright rejection without opportunity to rectify.

GJ-C3-001#cl-13.5 is marked superseded by GJ-C3-003 amendment effective 2020-01-22, so cannot be cited for 2025-12-02 application. | Check meter is mandatory only for systems >20 kW; proposed 12 kWp system is ≤20 kW, so check meter is optional, not required.
The clause makes check meters mandatory only for systems >20 kW; this 12 kWp system is ≤20 kW, so check meter is optional and rejection is incorrect.

DL-C3-004#cl-9.2b was superseded by DL-C3-015#cl-9.2b effective 2026-01-20, before the application date of 2026-05-08. | Under the current rule, twice-yearly changes are allowed; applicant made 2 changes with 3 months notice, which complies.
Clause allows adding connections twice per FY with 2-month notice; applicant gave 3-month notice and this is only the 3rd change, so limit not exceeded at application time.

DL-C3-004#cl-3.8 is superseded as of 2025-03-14; the amendment DL-C3-009#cl-3.8 (effective 2024-04-01) should apply. | Current rule limits GNM capacity to 5× sanctioned load (120kW×5=600kW max); 90kWp is compliant but wrong rule was cited.

Clause allows up to 5× sanctioned load (5×120kW=600kW max), and 90kWp complies, but the generator cited no subsidy amount despite PM-KUSUM/MNRE schemes potentially applying to GNM ground-mounted systems.

TN-C5-001#cl-2 applies only to LT consumers, but the applicant is LB-V Commercial (HT category with 150 kW contract demand). | The later 2021 order governs net feed-in eligibility and should have been cited for completeness.

TN-C5-001#cl-2 limits LT consumers to max 100% of sanctioned demand, but TN-C5-002#cl-I.2 allows up to 999 kW only for HT consumers; LT Commercial may be governed by older rule. | The cited clause references 999 kW cap which applies to net billing eligibility broadly, but LT-Commercial (LB-V) consumers may still be subject to TN-C5-001 restrictions not analyzed.

DL-C3-009#cl-3(6) is superseded as of application date 2026-09-06; DL-C3-015#cl-3.6 with updated 110 MW BRPL cap applies. | Under current rule, BRPL cap is 110 MW; cumulative 50 MW is within limit, so SLD waiver applies and rejection is unsupported.

Clause 3.6 governs SLD/network augmentation cost waiver eligibility, not grounds for application rejection; cumulative 50 MW is under BRPL's 110 MW limit. | The SLD waiver applies only to 11kV and below, but this project connects at 33 kV, so the clause doesn't justify rejection.

DL-C3-009#cl-3(6) was superseded before the application date (2026-04-28); the Seventh Amendment (DL-C3-015) with revised 100 MW cap for TPDDL is effective from 2026-01-20. | The applicable rule (DL-C3-015#cl-3.6) raising TPDDL's SLD waiver cap to 100 MW was not cited; at 105 MW cumulative, rejection may still be valid but under the current rule.
Cited clause governs SLD waiver caps, not grounds for rejection; cumulative 105 MW is within TPDDL's 100 MW limit only after this 400 kWp project, so rejection reasoning misapplies the threshold.

UP-C3-001 was superseded by UP-C3-002 effective 2019-01-04; application dated 2023-09-16 must use UP-C3-002#cl-6.2 with 75% threshold. | Applicable 2019 regulation allows 75% DT capacity (120 kW); cumulative 125 kW exceeds this, but correct rule was not cited.
75% of 160 kVA DT = 120 kW; resultant 125 kW exceeds this, but existing 110 kW already violates the limit before this application, so rejection reasoning is flawed.

DL-C3-004#cl-3.8 was superseded by DL-C3-009#cl-3.8 effective 2024-04-01, before the application date of 2024-06-28. | The amended rule allows GNM capacity up to 5x sanctioned load (max 10MW); 600kWp is within 5x100kW=500kW limit, so rejection appears incorrect.

Proposed 600 kWp is within 5x sanctioned load (5×100kW=500kW limit), but this applies to Ground Mounted GNM systems with participating consumers, not necessarily a single consumer scenario requiring rejection.

Registry confirms DL-C3-004#cl-3(8) was superseded before application date 2024-05-22; DL-C3-009#cl-3.8 (effective 2024-04-01) is the governing rule. | Amended rule limits ground-mounted GNM capacity to 5× sanctioned load (500 kW here); 600 kWp exceeds this, potentially blocking approval.

Clause 3.8 applies to Ground Mounted RE Systems, but the application is for rooftop solar, not ground-mounted. | Even if applicable, 600 kWp exceeds 5x sanctioned load (5×100kW=500kW), violating the cited capacity limit.

Clause 26 requires SDO to verify feasibility and issue intimation, but portal shows feasibility 'Not communicated' so approval is premature. | For LT installations ≤150kW, deemed feasibility under KA-C5-006 applies and was not considered.
Technical feasibility outcome is 'Not communicated by the licensee' and only 2 days elapsed; SDO verification per KA-C5-001#cl-26 is pending, so approval is premature.

DL-C3-006#cl-3.2 was superseded by DL-C3-015#cl-3.2 effective 2026-01-20, which extends VNM to all consumers. | The Seventh Amendment (effective 2026-01-20) makes VNM applicable to all NCT Delhi consumers, including commercial, but was not considered.

DL-C3-015#cl-3.2 expands VNM eligibility to ALL consumers in NCT Delhi, so NDLT commercial consumers are now eligible, contradicting the rejection. | Clause limits ground-mounted VNM capacity to 5x sanctioned load (5×20=100kWp max), but 150kWp was proposed; this violation was not cited as rejection reason.

Registry shows GJ-C3-003#cl-6.2 is superseded as of application date 2024-11-20. | Clause removes capacity restrictions for captive consumers; HTP-I industrial captive use at 80kWp should be permitted, not rejected.

Clause 6.2c-ii applies to captive consumers and Third Party Sale; this HTP-I Industrial consumer's net-metering application requires capacity check under clause 6.2c-iii or general industrial provisions. | For non-residential/non-MSME industrial consumers, capacity limit of 50% of sanctioned load applies; 80 kWp exceeds 50% of 100 kW (50 kW).

Registry shows GJ-C3-001#cl-13.5 is superseded as of application date 2025-04-24; GJ-C3-003 is the current regulation. | Proposed capacity is 18 kWp (≤20 kW), so check meter is optional, not mandatory; rule does not block or require approval action.
Clause states check meters are mandatory only for systems >20 kW; this 18 kWp system is ≤20 kW, so check meter is optional, not a blocking requirement.

KA-C5-006#cl-18 (effective 2025-12-01) supersedes KA-C5-001#cl-15, raising the check meter threshold to 50kWp. | The 30kWp system requires a check meter under superseding rule KA-C5-006#cl-18 (>50kWp threshold), but EPC shows 'Not provided'—should be flagged, not approved.

KA-C5-006#cl-18 applies to systems >50kWp, but proposed capacity is 30kWp, so clause doesn't govern this case. | KA-C5-001#cl-15 requires check meter for systems >17.5kW; 30kWp system lacks check meter, violating this rule.

GJ-C3-001#cl-5-proviso (65% limit) was superseded by GJ-C3-003 (2020 amendment) which removed the 65% cap, allowing 100% of transformer capacity. | Under amended rule, 100 kVA transformer allows 100 kW cumulative; 85 kW resultant capacity is within limit, so rejection is unsupported.
Resultant cumulative solar capacity (85 kW) exceeds transformer capacity (100 kVA limit), so the clause mandates rejection, not approval.
GJ-C3-003 (2020) superseded the 65% limit, allowing cumulative capacity up to 100% of transformer capacity; 70 kW ≤ 100 kVA passes.

Resultant cumulative capacity 70 kW exceeds 100% of 100 kVA transformer capacity, but clause allows cumulative capacity up to 100% of transformer capacity, so 70 kW should be allowed; however, the application requests 10 kWp which would make cumulative 70 kW, which is within 100 kVA limit, so arithmetic appears correct but existing 60 kW + 10 kW = 70 kW ≤ 100 kVA passes. | Generator failed to verify sanctioned load limit; proposed 10 kWp DC capacity exceeds 6 kW sanctioned load, violating typical net metering capacity restrictions.

Installations ≤150kW are deemed feasible per KA-C5-006#cl-4-note-ii; 9kWp qualifies, so no SDO verification needed. | Technical feasibility outcome is 'Not communicated'; approval cannot be granted before SDO communicates feasibility.

The cited clause provides deemed feasibility, but feasibility outcome has not been communicated and no approval decision can be issued at the Technical Feasibility stage. | SDO must verify technical feasibility and issue intimation letter before approval; this procedural requirement was not considered.

KA-C5-006#cl-18 (effective 2025-12-01) supersedes KA-C5-001#cl-15, raising check meter threshold to 50kWp. | Application should be rejected as 35kWp system lacks required check meter under current 50kWp threshold rule.

The 35 kWp system is below 50kWp threshold, so no check meter is required; however, KA-C5-001#cl-15 requires check meters for systems >17.5kW, which applies here. | System is 35kWp (>17.5kW), so KA-C5-001#cl-15 mandates a check meter, which the application lacks.

This clause requiring 0.2s accuracy was superseded by GJ-C3-003 amendment effective 2020-01-22, before application date 2025-12-23. | Current regulation requires Solar Meter accuracy of 1.0 class; application shows 1.0 class meter which complies. | System is 25kWp (>20kW), requiring mandatory check meter, but application shows 'Not provided' which should be the rejection basis.

System is 25 kWp (>20 kW), so check meter is mandatory per GJ-C3-003#cl-13.5-check, but rejection cites only meter accuracy class, not the missing check meter. | Solar Generation Meter (1.0) and Net Meter (0.5S) both meet the required accuracy classes; rejection on accuracy grounds is unsupported.

The clause limits capacity to 100% of sanctioned demand (8 kW), but the application requests Net Billing, not Net Feed-in; TN-C5-002 allows Net Billing up to sanctioned load, so 10 kWp exceeds 8 kW limit regardless, but wrong scheme was cited.

Clause permits net billing for all categories except hut/agriculture up to 999 kW; proposed 10 kWp is within sanctioned load of 8 kW per TN-C5-001#cl-2, and LA-1A Domestic is eligible, so rejection is unsupported.

DL-C3-006#cl-3.2 was superseded before the application date (2026-06-23) per the clause registry. | The current VNM guideline (DL-C3-015, effective 2026-01-20) extends VNM to all consumers, which should have been cited instead. | Even under the old rule, VNM was limited to domestic/charitable categories; the applicant is NDLT Non-Domestic with commercial participants.

VNM applicability clause does not override the system size limit; 120 kWp exceeds sanctioned load of 30 kW, violating standard capacity constraints. | Generator failed to verify compliance with capacity limits requiring solar capacity ≤ sanctioned load for net metering eligibility.

GJ-C3-001#cl-5.1 (65% limit) is superseded by GJ-C3-003 amendment which removed the 65% threshold. | The amended regulation removes the 65% cap, allowing cumulative capacity up to 100% of transformer capacity, which should have been cited.
Resultant cumulative solar capacity (55 kW) exceeds the 100 kVA transformer capacity limit per the cited clause, so application should be REJECTED, not APPROVED.

UP-C3-001 was superseded by UP-C3-002 effective 2019-01-04, before the application date of 2023-04-19. | Under the applicable 2019 regulation, 5 kWp does not exceed 100% of 4 kW connected demand; the rejection is arithmetically incorrect.

Proposed 5 kWp exceeds 100% of 4 kW sanctioned load, but UP-C3-002#cl-5.1 references 'connected/contracted demand' which is also 4 kW; however, the bill shows Connected Load as 4 kW, so 5 kWp (125%) violates the rule—rejection appears arithmetically correct but the generator failed to record computed values for verification.

DL-C3-009#cl-3(6) is superseded as of application date 2026-04-11; DL-C3-015#cl-3.6 is the effective rule. | Cumulative GNM capacity for BRPL is 95 MW, exceeding the 110 MW threshold limit, so SLD waiver does not apply and charges are due.
Cumulative GNM capacity for BRPL is 95 MW, and adding this 400 kWp project exceeds the 100 MW cap specified in DL-C3-015#cl-3.6, so SLD waiver does not apply.

Clause registry shows GJ-C3-003#cl-6.2 status is 'superseded' as of application date 2025-09-12. | Consumer is HTP-I Industrial, not residential/MSME; clause removes capacity restrictions only for captive consumers/Third Party Sale, not general industrial net metering.

HTP-I Industrial tariff does not qualify as captive consumer or third-party sale; cl-6.2c-ii applies only to captive consumers and third-party sale projects. | For non-residential/non-MSME consumers, capacity is limited to 50% of sanctioned load (150 kW), but 120 kWp proposed was not verified against this rule.

TN-C5-001#cl-2 applies to net feed-in connections, but the application requests Net Billing mode, which is governed by TN-C5-002. | TN-C5-002 permits net billing for all consumers irrespective of capacity limits applicable to net metering/feed-in, which was not considered.

Clause permits capacity up to 999 kW; 6 kWp proposed does not violate this, and TN-C5-001#cl-2 allows up to 100% of sanctioned load (4 kW), making 6 kWp exceed the 4 kW limit—but rejection cites wrong clause. | The actual applicable rule limiting capacity to 100% of sanctioned load (4 kW) was not cited as basis for rejection.

UP-C3-001 was superseded on 2019-01-04; application dated 2023-07-04 must use UP-C3-002#cl-6.2 with 75% threshold. | Under current UP-C3-002#cl-6.2, 75% of 100 kVA = 75 kW; 78 kW cumulative exceeds limit, but correct rule was not cited.

Resultant cumulative capacity 78 kW is 78% of 100 kVA DT, exceeding 75% limit by only 3 kW; however, existing 72 kW already equals 72%, so adding 6 kW violates the threshold—the rejection is actually correct but the generator failed to show the arithmetic computation.

DL-C3-004#cl-9.2b was superseded by DL-C3-015#cl-9.2b effective 2026-01-20, which allows twice per financial year, not once. | Under current rules, 2 changes/year allowed; applicant made 1 change, so adding a connection should be permitted.

Clause allows adding connections twice yearly with 2-month advance notice; applicant has made only 1 change but gave only 1-month notice instead of required 2 months—rejection valid but root cause misidentifies the violation.

Registry shows this clause was superseded as of 2026-03-30; the amended rule IN-C1-001#cl-annex1-ii-amended extends deadline to 31.12.2025, and CFA claim was received 2026-02-16. | Amended clause extending Phase-II claims deadline to 31.12.2025 for installed/inspected applications was not considered.

Phase II applications have CFA deadline of 31.12.2025; CFA claim received 2026-02-16 is after deadline, but generator garbled the rule text and cited October 2024 deadline which applies to Phase I only. | Generator failed to cite IN-C1-011 which confirms Phase II applications submitted before 13 Feb 2024 remain eligible for CFA under revised subsidy rates.

DL-C3-009#cl-3(6) is superseded as of application date 2026-05-18; DL-C3-015 is the current regulation. | Current rule DL-C3-015 sets TPDDL SLD waiver cap at 100 MW; cumulative capacity is 120 MW, exceeding the limit. | Even under cited rule, TPDDL cap was 50 MW; 120 MW cumulative capacity exceeds this threshold.
Cumulative TPDDL capacity is 120 MW, exceeding the 100 MW threshold in DL-C3-015#cl-3.6, so SLD waiver no longer applies and approval is unsupported.

Clause GJ-C3-001#cl-13.5 was superseded by GJ-C3-003 amendment effective 2020-01-22, before application date 2025-05-15. | Superseding regulation requires Solar Meter accuracy 1.0 class, but proposal shows 0.5S which may not meet current requirements for solar generation meter.

Solar Generation Meter must be 1.0 class or better per regulation, but EPC proposes 0.5S which exceeds requirements; however, approval cites meter accuracy rule without verifying if this is the actual blocking issue at 'Meter Installation' stage. | The cited clause governs meter accuracy standards but does not constitute grounds for full application approval; it only confirms meter compliance, not overall eligibility.

KA-C5-006 states installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible without requiring feasibility reports, superseding KA-C5-001#cl-26 SDO verification requirement. | Technical Feasibility Outcome is 'Not communicated'; approval cannot be granted when feasibility is still pending.

Note-ii applies only to LT installations per Note-i, but application is LT-3 Commercial which requires SDO verification per KA-C5-001#cl-26 before approval. | SDO must verify technical feasibility and issue intimation letter before approval; feasibility outcome is 'Not communicated' so approval is premature.

Registry confirms this clause was superseded by 2026-02-14; the amended rule IN-C1-001#cl-annex1-ii-amended extends Phase II claims deadline to 31.12.2025, which still covers the 2026-01-15 claim date issue but supersedes the cited October 2024 cutoff. | The amended rule extending CFA eligibility for Phase II applications to 31.12.2025 was not considered; CFA claim received 2026-01-15 may still miss this deadline but rejection reasoning cited wrong clause.

Phase II applications are admissible for CFA if claim received till 31.12.2025; CFA claim received 2026-01-15 is after deadline, but generator misquoted October 2024 deadline which applies only to Phase I.

DL-C3-006#cl-3.2 was superseded by DL-C3-015#cl-3.2 effective 2026-01-20, which permits VNM for all Delhi consumers. | The current VNM rule (effective 2026-01-20) allows VNM for all NCT Delhi consumers, making domestic housing society eligible.

DL-C3-015#cl-3.2 permits VNM for all Delhi consumers including domestic, so citing it as rejection basis contradicts the clause's actual permissive content. | Clause 3.8 limits ground-mounted VNM capacity to 5x sanctioned load (150 kW max here), but proposed 200 kWp exceeds this—rejection should cite capacity violation, not VNM applicability.
